asset: Authority Nexus wormhole anchor — front, back, top, bottom, side reference

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a production-quality five-view orthographic 2D reference sheet for future 3D modeling of the AUTHORITY NEXUS WORMHOLE ANCHOR in Stellar Syndicates.
Input image: the APPROVED intact powered Authority Nexus design. This is the sole design reference. Translate this same structure into front, back, top, bottom and side views. Do not redesign it. Show the intact operating state in every view.

PRESERVE THE DESIGN:
- A broad, thick concentric terraced orbital port surrounding a large circular wormhole aperture. Keep the reference's faceted outer terraces, recessed empty cargo berths, glass-fronted port halls, freight containers and dark graphite understructure.
- Exactly FOUR tall stabilizer pylons at the four cardinal positions, front, rear, left and right. Each has an elegant fluted ivory Art Deco shell, brass framing and nested focusing coils around an exposed cyan-white power spine. Keep the same tower heights and proportions as the reference.
- Four broad physical armored power conduits connect these pylons to four aligned anchor emitters on the inner containment ring. Cyan inset conduit segments, brass couplings, repeated induction coils, heat sinks and coolant pipes make the power system visibly functional.
- The horizontal wormhole is a contained violet-indigo spiral with a dark throat. Four SHORT cyan-violet field tethers grip its circumference. The transit center is entirely unobstructed. No central reactor, mast, solid floor, spokes, shutter or mechanical iris inside the aperture.
- Authority materials: pale ivory titanium and ceramic armor, restrained brass, graphite machinery, fine warm amber windows and sparse cyan service lights. Fine seams, panel lines, subtle wear. No weapon turrets.
- The purpose of this station is to expend power continuously to hold the wormhole open. Preserve the visible connection from stabilizer pylons through feeds and emitters to the portal rim.

LAYOUT: one high-resolution 3:2 landscape reference sheet on a plain white or extremely light neutral-gray background. Exactly FIVE separate fully visible orthographic views. Upper row: two large equal-sized plan views, TOP at left and BOTTOM at right. Lower row: three clean equal-sized elevation views, FRONT, BACK, SIDE, from left to right. Large clean margins and gutters; no station parts touch the labels or sheet edges. Keep geometry and dimensional proportions consistent across every view. A modest small charcoal sans-serif title at the top reads exactly "AUTHORITY NEXUS — WORMHOLE ANCHOR". Each view has its label centered directly beneath it, exactly once: "TOP", "BOTTOM", "FRONT", "BACK", "SIDE".

ORTHOGRAPHIC REQUIREMENTS:
TOP: true perpendicular overhead plan, circular inner ring, not an ellipse. All four stabilizer positions and four power routes are unambiguous. Look straight down into the open active wormhole. Do not use a tilted overhead beauty-shot camera.
BOTTOM: true perpendicular underside view of this SAME station, matching the same radial footprint, collar diameter, four structural roots and faceted terraces. Show a fully designed engineering underside: layered ivory armor panels, graphite radial support webs outside the aperture, power-plant housings, broad ribbed radiator panels, heavy coolant lines and service hatches. The pylons stand on the TOP only; do not add another set of downward-facing towers on the bottom. The underside is not a duplicate of the upper cargo deck: no upside-down cranes, containers or copied windows. The center stays open and the reverse side of the contained violet energy is visible through the hole. No solid plate covering the portal.
FRONT: straight-on horizontal elevation looking across the station plane from its designated front. A wide thick stepped disk, the foreground pylon, side pylons, port halls and underside radiators are visible; correctly occlude the rear tower where geometry requires.
BACK: the exact opposite horizontal elevation. Reveal the reverse armor faces and rear maintenance access of the same upper structures and ring. Do not add or remove architectural masses.
SIDE: a perpendicular 90-degree horizontal elevation showing the matching profile, pylon arrangement and port halls.
All three elevations are genuinely EDGE-ON, not low-angle perspective or three-quarter views. The wormhole lies HORIZONTALLY inside the station: in elevations its energy can show only as a narrow inset violet line where not occluded. Never turn it into a large vertical portal disk or show the whole spiral in an elevation. Model the tower height and station thickness consistently. Natural geometric occlusion is correct; do not move hidden pylons aside to display them.

STYLE: precise colored hard-surface concept rendering with readable construction and texture detail suitable for 3D mesh and material work. Soft neutral studio lighting consistent across views, enough fill to see all underside details, no heavy external shadows, clean crisp contours. Maintain the elegant monumental civic architecture of the approved reference rather than generic industrial scaffolding. Restrained emission keeps the machinery visible.

AVOID: extra views, isometric beauty shots, damaged or destroyed states, another hub design, old twelve-docking-arm silhouette, new towers, huge bloom, fog, stars, nebulae, planets, ships, people, weapons fire, dimension lines, scale bars, callout arrows, logos, watermark, UI or extra text.

Make ONE localized geometric correction to the supplied five-view Authority Nexus reference sheet. Preserve the entire TOP, BOTTOM, FRONT and BACK panels exactly, and preserve the title, all labels, white background, panel layout, image dimensions, material palette and image quality.

Correct ONLY the lower-right panel labeled SIDE. The TOP view establishes four tall vertical stabilizer pylons at the four cardinal compass points. In a true 90-degree side elevation, the nearest side pylon must therefore stand directly in the CENTER foreground, with the opposite far pylon aligned behind it and hidden. The current SIDE panel incorrectly omits this central foreground pylon and shows only the left and right silhouette towers.

Add the missing foreground center stabilizer tower to the SIDE elevation. Match the existing FRONT and BACK elevation's center tower HEIGHT, WIDTH, fluted ivory Art Deco architecture, brass focusing coils, cyan vertical power spine and broad anchored base, while depicting the side-facing pylon of this same station. This is not a new fifth tower; it is the already-existing cardinal pylon that the side projection should reveal. Retain the currently visible left and right silhouette pylons and underlying disk, port halls and radiator blocks unchanged. The corrected SIDE panel should show THREE visible tower silhouettes: one centered and one at either side, with the fourth tower naturally occluded directly behind the center one.

Keep the corrected panel perfectly edge-on and orthographic. Keep the wormhole horizontal, visible only as a slim violet line where not occluded. Do not show a face-on portal circle. The central pylon is above the deck, with its root integrated into the center foreground of the port, not a detached tower floating over it. Keep every full station inside its panel and preserve all five view labels exactly once. No other changes.
